title: Operator self-service utility kit and step synthesis
creator: Marina Karpov
description: Problem: On-call and tier-1 support spend too much time invoking ad-hoc admin scripts and switching contexts during incidents. Existing runbook artifacts are prose-heavy and require engineer intervention to execute. Goal: Ship a lightweight operator self-service utility kit that exposes vetted admin actions as composable step templates. These step templates should be runnable from the operator console or CLI as first-class 'task' primitives (runbooks-as-tasks), include safety gates and auditing, and integrate with existing support automation triggers (PagerDuty, Slack commands). Deliverables: (1) operator-utility binary (CLI) and HTTP endpoint for gated actions; (2) a library of step templates for common workflows (cache flush, model migration toggle, restart worker pool, fallback routing); (3) a web UI in Console to discover and execute allowed steps; (4) audit events persisted to logging/KV and surfaced in Console traces.
acceptance_criteria: Operator utility exposes at least six approved admin step templates that replicate current runbook run sequences
Steps support dry-run mode and explicit confirmation prompts for destructive actions
Every executed step emits audit metadata (who, when, parameters, success/failure) to the centralized logging pipeline
Console shows a discovery surface for available steps with per-step docs, RBAC gating, and execution history
CLI and Console executions can be wired into existing support automation (Slack slash /ops-run, PagerDuty runbook hooks) without custom glue
Performance: typical non-destructive steps complete within SLOs (<= 3s for queries, <= 30s for orchestrated tasks) and do not increase error rates in runtime metrics
tasks: Draft step-template schema and validation rules (param types, safety labels, dry-run flag)
Prototype operator utility: subcommands list, run, dry-run, audit-report
Implement RBAC check integration with Console auth tokens and SSO groups
Build Console discovery panel and execution modal with confirmation flow
Add audit event emitter and hook into existing logging ingestion (telemetry team)
Create 6 canonical step templates and test harness (cache purge, worker restart, model pin, kv prune, route fallback, metrics rollup)
End-to-end test and runbook->task conversion script for 10 existing runbooks
Documentation: Confluence runbook migration guide and runbook-to-step checklist
Create a lightweight /ops-run Slack slash command with rate-limits and approval flow
progress_updates: 2026-02-16: Discovery completed with SRE and On-call rotation leads. Identified top 10 frequent runbook actions and 4 high-risk destructive patterns.
2026-02-22: Spike: CLI prototype (operator-util v0.1) implemented; supports dry-run and audit event stubbing. Repo: github.com/redwood-inference/operator-util (PR #412)
2026-02-27: Security review kickoff with InfoSec. Decided to gate destructive steps behind SSO group and MFA prompt. Recording: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/OPS-SELF-SVC
2026-03-03: Console mockups reviewed by PM and UX. Chose modal-first flow with per-step docs and inline dry-run toggle. Design doc: https://drive.google.com/ops-step-design
2026-03-07: Integrated audit emitter with logging pipeline staging. Events appear in Kibana under indices ops-audit-*. Initial schema attached to PR #438

2026-03-10: Alpha release to internal SRE cohort. First 3 step templates published (cache purge, worker restart, model pin). Feedback: confirmation copy needs clearer rollback guidance. Follow-up task created.
notes: Risk: Need to ensure steps cannot be chained by non-privileged users to form destructive sequences. Mitigation: step-level safety labels and rate-limiting middleware.
Trade-off: Scripting full orchestration language increases power but also risk. We'll start with composable atomic steps and a vetted orchestration builder for power users in a future cycle.
Next steps: implement improved confirmation copy, add rollback helper to worker restart, run tabletop with rotational on-call team on 2026-03-16.
